Key observations from test image:
- Severe stem damage at/near soil line
- Very dark brown to black stem discoloration at base
- Tiny black specks visible on stem surface (resembling charcoal dust)
- Plants appear dead/dying with collapsed stems
- Dark rotted tissue with possible microsclerotia

Top candidates: **Charcoal_Rot** (dark stems with tiny black specks/microsclerotia near soil), **Phytophthora** (chocolate-brown stem discoloration from soil line up), **Rhizoctonia** (stem rot at soil line).

Let me view reference images for the top candidates.

Analysis complete. The test image shows:
- Close-up of stem bases near soil line with very dark (near-black) discoloration
- Tiny black specks visible on stem surfaces — characteristic microsclerotia resembling charcoal dust
- Plants dead/collapsed at late season stage
- Reddish-orange inner tissue visible where stems are broken

**Charcoal_Rot** matches precisely: "stems near soil surface appear gray with tiny black specks or dots resembling charcoal dust; small black spots (pycnidia/microsclerotia) dispersed across stem surface; reddish-brown discoloration in vascular tissues."

Rhizoctonia shows reddish-orange sunken lesions (not matching). Phytophthora shows chocolate-brown discoloration extending up the stem (possible but the charcoal-dust specks are distinctive here).
